findings.text: The rename sweep also flipped an operator. In `acornLooseChannelScore`, the a < b branch changed from `scaleBy(b, 96) - a` to `scaleBy(b, 96) + a`. This is not part of the rename, and it changes the exported function's return value whenever a < b and a != 0: (1,2) returned 193 and now returns 195; (3,4) returned 383 and now returns 389. It violates A1 ('behaviour is unchanged'), A2 ('Nothing else changes'), the contract ('Renames keep behaviour') and the non-goal 'No unrelated changes'. The direction text also requires sweeps to stay mechanical. The green lanes do not detect it: packages/acorn has no test directory, and goldens record only export names, params and called helpers, so regeneration cannot show an operator change.
evidence: tools/gen-goldens.ts:14-24 (goldens record name, params and calls only, not operators)
Of the 57 changed files under packages, this is the only one that differs from its base version with acornBase replaced by acornRoot

directives: In packages/acorn/src/loose-channel.ts:12, restore `scaleBy(b, 96) - a` so that the only change to that line's file is acornBase → acornRoot.
Rerun `node tools/gen-goldens.ts` and commit whatever it produces. Do not edit goldens by hand.

Before resubmitting, confirm that every changed file under packages/ matches its base version with acornBase replaced by acornRoot. The lanes and goldens cannot detect an operator change, so this comparison is the check.
reasons: A1 not met. The rename is complete: no `acornBase` remains anywhere in the tree, including packages/acorn/legacy. But 'behaviour is unchanged' is false, because `acornLooseChannelScore` returns different values when a < b and a != 0.

A2 not met. The golden file was regenerated correctly: the executor's regeneration check was byte-identical, and the golden diff I read shows only acornBase → acornRoot. But 'Nothing else changes' is false because of the same operator flip.
The passing unit lane is not evidence for either clause here, because packages/acorn has no tests and goldens do not record operators.

premises.claim: Goldens record export names, parameters and called helpers only, so they cannot detect an arithmetic operator change.
The only change beyond the rename is the operator on line 12 of loose-channel.ts.
